Good morning from the hills of Judea, near Jerusalem.

We’re here visiting friends, and last night we joined them for my first-ever Thanksgiving dinner. Who would have thought I’d finally get the full experience - stuffed turkey, pumpkin pie, and all - right here in Israel?

We went around the table and shared what we were thankful for. Of course, we thanked God for our spouses, our children, and our extended families.

Somehow, we made it through the entire meal without talking about politics! What did come up was the growing need for more teaching on Israel. People spoke of friends abroad who know very little about Israel and of churches where many who call themselves “New Testament believers” show little interest in what Scripture says about it.

We agreed that the problem runs deeper. It starts with a heretical approach to Scripture that turns God’s promises to Israel into spiritual symbols. Nearly 30 percent of the Bible is prophetic. How much of it do we explain away when we refuse to take the prophets at their word?

Erasing Israel from your theology is erasing prophecy from your Bible.

This morning, while I was still lying in bed, I thought about the two disciples on the road to Emmaus, about five miles from where we’re staying. They had hoped Yeshua would redeem Israel, and they thought that hope had died with Him. Because they had failed to believe the prophets, they missed the very purpose of His coming and the promise of His resurrection. That’s why they were walking in sorrow even as the risen Messiah Himself walked beside them!

“O foolish ones, and slow of heart to believe in all that the prophets have spoken! Ought not the Christ to have suffered these things and to enter into His glory?”
(Luke 24:25–26)

Yeshua said all that the prophets have spoken. That includes God’s promises to Israel. Why would He expect any less of us today?

Awaiting His Soon Return,

Amir
